directories.modules: Feature modules (one folder per domain), each an Elysia plugin
directories.config: Application configuration — the only place that reads process.env (Bun.env)
directories.plugins: Cross-cutting Elysia plugins (auth, error handling, CORS, logging) composed with .use()
directories.database: Drizzle client, schema/ (table definitions), migrations/ (drizzle-kit output), shared DB utilities
directories.types: Backend-only types (shared types go in packages/shared-types)

entryFiles.index.ts: Builds the app as ONE fluent chain (`export const app = new Elysia().use(...)...`) and `export type App = typeof app` for the Eden treaty client; calls listen()
entryFiles.drizzle.config.ts: drizzle-kit config (at apps/backend/, next to package.json)

files.routes.ts: Elysia chained plugin: `new Elysia({ prefix, name }).get(...).post(...)`. Parses request, validates with TypeBox (`t`), calls the service, returns the response. No business logic, no queries.
files.model.ts: TypeBox schemas (`t.Object`, `t.Union([t.Literal(..), ...])`) for request/response — the single validator, no second one
files.repository.ts: Database access with Drizzle (query builder or sql`` template with parameters)

modulePattern.schemaLocation: Drizzle tables live in database/schema/ (one file per domain, re-exported from database/schema/index.ts); modules import from there

requirements: Routes (Elysia plugins) handle HTTP only — no business logic and no database queries
Repositories contain all database queries (Drizzle); never string-concatenate SQL
Each feature gets its own folder under modules/ and is mounted with .use() in index.ts
The app is one fluent chain and exports `type App = typeof app`; never call `app.get(...)` on a separate statement — it discards the route types and Eden collapses to {}
Conditional routes and static-file fallbacks go inside a handler, not outside the chain
Validation uses TypeBox only; spell unions out with t.Union([t.Literal(...)]) rather than mapping over a constant
Cross-cutting concerns are Elysia plugins (derive/onBeforeHandle/onError) in plugins/, not Express-style middleware chains
Migrations are generated by drizzle-kit into database/migrations/; schema changes are a major improvement needing tech-architect approval
legacy: Projects with Vibe Start before 2026-10-07 may keep their existing backend (e.g. Node/Express with controller/service/repository/routes and middleware/). Audit them against their existing structure as advisory; do not convert.
